0.0.n: A standard greeting used mainly during the daytime.

0.2.n: An abbreviated name for the show ポルカの伝説.

0.3.n: Combined with the show name, this identifies the team the speaker belongs to.

0.4.n: Links the staff group to 井筒, identifying him as a member.

0.5.n: This is the speaker’s family name.

0.6.n: A polite sentence ending used here to introduce oneself; Japanese leaves out “I.”

1.0.n: Sets the time for the test.

1.1.n: Marks 今日 as the topic: the speaker is explaining what will happen today.

1.2.n: This is the name of the person being kept unaware of the test.

1.3.n: Added after ポルカ to address or mention her respectfully.

1.4.n: With 内緒, marks the person who is not being told.

1.5.n: In ポルカさんに内緒で, it indicates that Polka will not be told.

1.6.n: Connects 内緒 to the action, describing how the test will be conducted.

1.7.n: Before a noun, ある introduces something specific without saying exactly what it is.

1.8.n: Refers to checking whether something is true or works as expected.

1.9.n: Marks 検証 as what the speaker will carry out.

1.10.n: Polite form of する; here it announces a planned action.

2.0.n: Signals a transition from the introduction to the show.

2.2.n: Refers to the day of this episode.

2.3.n: Links 今日 to the show title, indicating today’s episode.

2.4.n: This name appears as part of the show title ポルカの伝説.

2.5.n: Links ポルカ and 伝説 within the title, making it Polka’s legend.

2.6.n: Together with ポルカの, this forms the show’s title, Legend of Polka.

2.7.n: Marks today’s show as what viewers are invited to enjoy.

2.8.n: お + the verb stem 楽しみ + ください makes a polite invitation to viewers.

0.lit: Hello, [I] am Izutsu of the Pol-Den staff.
0.tip: Japanese commonly omits “I” in introductions when the speaker’s identity is clear.

1.lit: As for today, without telling Polka, [we] will conduct a certain test.
1.tip: Someone + に内緒で means doing something without telling that person.

2.lit: Now then, please enjoy today’s Legend of Polka.
2.tip: お楽しみください is a polite invitation often used to introduce a show or event.
